description:
Housing units (H1) and tenure of occupied housing units (H4 — owned with a mortgage or loan, owned free and clear, renter occupied). `pct_owned`, `pct_rented` and `pct_vacant_2020` are this build's own shares, named apart from the ACS housing collections' `pct_owner_occupied` and `pct_vacant_units` so the two are never selected as if they were one column.

All **85,184** census tracts in the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics File](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/about/rdo/summary-files.html) (DHC), tables H1 and H4. The DHC is a 100% count from every return, the same survey family as the [blocks](../../blocks/collection.json) collection's P.L. 94-171 redistricting counts, read with the same per-state zip, Latin-1 geoheader and `LOGRECNO` join — but a different table set: blocks carries race, Hispanic origin, voting-age population and housing occupancy; this carries age, sex, household type and tenure, at block-groups and tracts rather than blocks.

**No margin of error, no coefficient of variation.** A 100% count carries no sampling error, so there is nothing here to estimate the uncertainty of — every column is the Bureau's tabulated count, full stop.

**Differential privacy.** The 2020 Census protects confidentiality with a disclosure avoidance system that injects statistical noise calibrated to a privacy-loss budget, most at block level and least at state level (state population totals are held exact; smaller geographies and smaller counts carry more). A block group or tract's individual cells can be off by a few people even though the file shows no margin of error; see the Census Bureau's [disclosure avoidance documentation](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/decade/2020/planning-management/process/disclosure-avoidance.html) and the [DHC technical documentation](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial/2020/technical-documentation/complete-tech-docs/demographic-and-housing-characteristics-file-and-demographic-profile/2020census-demographic-and-housing-characteristics-file-and-demographic-profile-techdoc.pdf) (Chapter 4, "Confidentiality of the Data").

This sits beside the American Community Survey collections at the same geography, not in a separate decennial group: [Income & Poverty](../tract-income/collection.json), [People & Education](../tract-people/collection.json), [Housing & Rent](../tract-housing/collection.json), [Commuting & Connectivity](../tract-connectivity/collection.json), [Health, Disability & Income by Race](../tract-wellbeing/collection.json). All of them share this collection's `geoid` and geometry and join 1:1 on `geoid` — but **do not subtract one from the other**. This is a different measurement: a 2020 Census 100% count with injected noise, not a 2020–2024 ACS 5-year sample estimate with a margin of error. The same theme at the other geography this batch covers is [Tenure (2020 Census) — Block Groups](../../block-groups/bg-tenure-dec2020/collection.json).

The PMTiles archive is one band, the collection's own features at every zoom (`tylertoo tiles`, not the county/tract pyramid the ACS collections use) — bg and tract are the two finest geographies this batch covers and there is no coarser DHC band to step up to yet. There are no `*_moe` columns to exclude: this is a 100% count, not an estimate, so there is nothing to exclude.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them.

concepts.title: 2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics File

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 11-character census tract GEOID — state (2) + county (3) + tract (6), e.g. `29510102200`. Joins the block-group collections on `substr(geoid, 1, 11)` and the block collection on `substr(geoid, 1, 11)`. Matches `GEOID` in the 2024 cartographic boundary tract file; the ACS `1400000US` prefix is stripped.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: Human-readable name from the cartographic boundary tract file: `NAMELSAD`, `NAMELSADCO`, `STATE_NAME` — "Census Tract 34.06, San Joaquin County, California".

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state code, carried from the DHC geoheader's own per-state build rather than read off the boundary files (tools/build_dhc.py's `STATES` list).

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND / 1e6` from the cartographic boundary file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: total_housing_units
table:columns.description: Total housing units (H1 cell `P0010001` per the geoheader's own count, table `H1`, "Total"). Not the ACS housing collections' `housing_units`.

table:columns.name: occupied_total
table:columns.description: Occupied housing units (H4 cell `H0040001`, "Total:" — the universe of H4 is occupied housing units). Equals `total_households` in the household collection at this geography.

table:columns.name: owned_with_mortgage
table:columns.description: Occupied housing units owned with a mortgage or a loan (H4).

table:columns.name: owned_free_clear
table:columns.description: Occupied housing units owned free and clear, with no mortgage or loan (H4).

table:columns.name: pct_owned
table:columns.description: Share of occupied housing units that are owner-occupied, with or without a mortgage (`(owned_with_mortgage + owned_free_clear) / occupied_total`), this build's own derived share — not the ACS housing collections' `pct_owner_occupied`.

table:columns.name: pct_rented
table:columns.description: Share of occupied housing units that are renter-occupied (`renter_occupied / occupied_total`), this build's own derived share.

table:columns.name: pct_vacant_2020
table:columns.description: Share of all housing units that are vacant (`(total_housing_units - occupied_total) / total_housing_units`), this build's own derived share — named apart from the ACS housing collections' `pct_vacant_units` so the two are never selected as if they were one column.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary census tract file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the census tract into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.

tract-tenure-dec2020-tiles.title: Tenure (2020 Census) — Census Tracts (PMTiles)
tract-tenure-dec2020-tiles.description: Vector tiles rendered from the collection's GeoParquet for map display, layer 'tract-tenure-dec2020'. The collection description states what each zoom band carries.

tract-tenure-dec2020.title: Tenure (2020 Census) — Census Tracts (GeoParquet, national)
tract-tenure-dec2020.description: GeoParquet with the collection's features and attributes. Every column carries a description in this collection's table:columns.

thumbnail.title: Tenure (2020 Census) — Census Tracts rendered with the default style
thumbnail.description: A rendered card of the collection's own data, drawn with the default style.

styles/default.title: Owner-occupied housing
styles/default.description: Share of occupied housing units that are owner-occupied (H4), pale pink to deep magenta -- a 100% count, not the ACS housing collections' pct_owner_occupied estimate. Neither blue nor green: connectivity owns the blue ramp and age the green one, and a blue-green tested too close to connectivity at card size. Pink is the one hue path no other default style in this catalog uses. Measured over all 84,630 tracts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 40%/55%/65%/75%/85%, which fall at the 18th/32nd/45th/61st/83rd percentile of the national distribution.

styles/vacant.title: Vacant housing units
styles/vacant.description: Vacant share of all housing units (H1 minus H4's occupied total), cream to deep red -- a 100% count, not the ACS housing collections' pct_vacant_units estimate. Measured over all 84,729 tracts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 3%/6%/10%/15%/25%, which fall at the 12th/42nd/68th/84th/94th percentile of the national distribution.

source-dhc-states.title: 2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics File (DHC) — state directories
source-dhc-states.description: The 52 state archives (`{State_Name}/{ab}2020.dhc.zip`) this collection's counts were read from. Each archive holds a pipe-delimited Latin-1 geoheader plus 44 segment files joined on `LOGRECNO`; this collection reads segments carrying H1 and H4 and filters the geoheader to `SUMLEV = '140'`, `GEOCOMP = '00'`. Served by census.gov.

doc-dhc-techdoc.title: 2020 Census DHC and Demographic Profile — Technical Documentation
doc-dhc-techdoc.description: Chapter 3 (Data Dictionary) gives the table shells; Chapter 4 (Confidentiality of the Data) is the source for this collection's differential-privacy known issue. Served by census.gov.

doc-dhc-table-matrix.title: 2020 Census DHC Table Matrix
doc-dhc-table-matrix.description: Table ID, segment number and field position for every DHC table — the spreadsheet this build's field positions (tools/build_dhc.py) were derived from and verified against the real per-state files' field counts. Served by census.gov.

doc-disclosure-avoidance.title: 2020 Census Disclosure Avoidance System
doc-disclosure-avoidance.description: The Census Bureau's own explanation of the differential-privacy system that injects noise into every 2020 Census data product, this one included. Served by census.gov.

source-cartographic-boundaries.title: 2024 cartographic boundary file — census tracts (1:500,000, national)
source-cartographic-boundaries.description: The same boundary file the ACS collections at this geography join to — reused, not re-downloaded, so a DHC row and an ACS row for the same `geoid` always share the same geometry.
